name: Ong Pak-wai
languages: Cantonese (the Toisan speech of his home district), read and written
Spanish (enough to bargain, from the California placers)
equipment: A quilted blue cotton jacket and trousers, a felt hat and good American boots, bought in Sacramento
Repeating rifle (Winchester 1873), carried openly since the Miners' Union resolution
A surveyor's level and a hand compass in a leather case, and a hundred-foot chain
A contract with the DA&P for the grading of Hollowell Cut, in English and Chinese, and the company's daybook of every man, every day's work, every scrip payment and every shortfall
A copy of a letter to the Chinese Consul General in San Francisco, not yet sent
An abacus, a brush, an inkstone and a stick of ink
A tin of tea and a pipe
features: Two Tongues (Immigrant origin: he speaks, reads and writes Cantonese and English and speaks some Spanish; he has advantage on Insight and Perception to follow a conversation the speakers think he cannot understand, which in Argent is most of them; in any Chinese community from San Francisco to Denver his district association will give him a meal, a bed, work and the news)

Trailcraft (Scout: he is never lost on terrain he has crossed, finds water each day without a check, follows a trail at a normal pace with a Survival check and reads from it how many, how long ago and how loaded; a party he guides cannot become lost)

Long Shot (Scout: attacking at long range with a Longarm imposes no disadvantage if he Aimed first that turn; his proficiency bonus is doubled for Perception checks to spot something more than 300 ft away)
Ghost on the Range (Scout, 2nd level: in natural terrain he can Hide as a bonus action, even when only lightly obscured, and leaves no trail anyone without Trailcraft can follow unless he chooses to)
Path: Guide (Scout, 3rd level: his party travels at a hard pace without exhaustion, finds forage for its animals on any terrain that has any, and has advantage on saves against weather)
Ability Score Improvement (Scout, 4th level: +1 Dexterity, +1 Wisdom)
Extra Attack (Scout, 5th level: he attacks twice when he takes the Attack action)

Riding the Rails (Railroad Man background: he has graded railroad from the Sierra to the Rockies; every grading camp and section house on a line he has worked knows his name, and he reads a grade, a cut or a rock face like a page)

personality.traits: I am exact. I keep accounts of everything, including insults. I am patient until the moment I am not.
personality.ideals: A contract is a contract. My men did the work; my men will be paid; my men will not be blamed for what other men did.
personality.bonds: The sixty-one men of my company, most of them from villages near mine, whose families in Toisan eat because they work. Above all the two youngest, Leung Ah-sing and Chan Yiu, nineteen and seventeen, whose fathers made me promise to bring them home.
personality.flaws: I am proud, and I do not forgive. I have made up my mind about the Miners' Union and every man in it, and some of them do not deserve it.

appearance: A slender, upright Chinese man of forty with a lined, serious face, a long queue wound under his hat, spectacles for close work and a surveyor's weathered hands. He speaks quietly and precisely and looks at a cut or a slope the way a doctor looks at a wound.
backstory: Ong Pak-wai came to California from Toisan in 1858, worked placer claims in the Sierra, and in 1865 joined the Central Pacific's crews blasting the line over the Sierra Nevada, where he learned English, surveying and powder from an engineer who noticed he could read a slope better than he could. By 1869 he was a headman with his own company of graders. He has graded railroad from Nevada to Colorado since. The DA&P contracted his company to cut the grade at Hollowell Cut because they are the best and the cheapest, and paid them, like everyone, in scrip. The Miners' Union in Argent has voted that no Chinese may live or work in the basin; his company camps at the Cut, four miles out, and does not come into town. He has heard men in the Argent saloons saying that if anything goes wrong on the grade it will be the Chinese crew's fault, and he has started carrying a rifle where his men and everyone else can see it.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Ong is the party's expert on the grade and the pass, and the most important witness in sl-scenario-002. On Wednesday morning (sl-scenario-002) a rockslide comes down on his camp before dawn and kills Leung Ah-sing and Chan Yiu. By the time the party arrives he has examined the slope and found the drill holes and Vulcan powder wrappers above the cut where his men never worked (Clues E1, D1); he will show the party if they come to the Cut and treat him as a contractor and a witness rather than a suspect. His daybook is evidence of the scrip shortfalls behind the strike (Clue F2). In sl-scenario-003 his crew lines the track at the Cut when the train passes, and he is the one who sees the runaway car and can get to the Blind Tom switch first. In sl-scenario-004 he can find a route around Brannock's forts at the Narrows (Trailcraft and Path: Guide, and ten years of reading grades). Never make him a victim waiting to be rescued: he has his own plan, his own evidence and his own letter to the consul, and if the party is too slow he will act without them.
dmNotes.voice: Precise, formal English, a little old-fashioned, learned from engineers and contracts: I regret, it is my understanding, in accordance with. Dry humour. He addresses men by surname and title until they earn otherwise. Speaks Cantonese to his foremen, quickly.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: clear his company of the rockslide, and get justice for Leung Ah-sing and Chan Yiu. Secondary: be paid in full, in coin, for the grading of Hollowell Cut, $4,100 owed. Tertiary: finish the contract and leave Colorado alive.
dmNotes.secrets: On Tuesday night at about nine, from the ridge above the Cut, his foreman Yee Kam-ling saw three riders leading three loaded mules turn off the grade up Blind Tom Gulch toward the old mine, where nobody has worked in two years, and come back at midnight without the load. Ong noted it in the daybook because it was odd. He does not know what it means (Clue G3).
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: courteous, reserved, testing. He will judge them by whether they listen. Toward Winfield Coburn: respect for the engineer, contempt for the scrip. Toward Roy Brannock: he graded for a man like Brannock once and knows the type. Toward Mercy Pengelly: genuine warmth; she was the first person from Argent to bring bread. Toward Llew Treharne: he knows Llew voted against the resolution, and has not decided whether it matters.
